comments.body:
**Claude finished @itsHabib's task in 6m 34s** —— [View job](https://github.com/itsHabib/workbench/actions/runs/30598226848)

---
### Review: feat(review): add opt-in exact-head tier-aware policy

- [x] Gather context and understand request
- [x] Read observe.go, main.go, policy.go, reviewroute.go
- [x] Read tests and canary policy
- [x] Analyze and post review findings

---

### Summary

All findings from the three prior review passes are correctly addressed in the current code — parentheses, `proved_safe` schema validation, `stale`-overwrites-`failed` comment, `runDecide` pre-network validation, `sortedUnique` unexported, `validLowerHex` naming, `proofSubstitutesPanel` cycle-guard comment, `actorMatches` copilot alias, and the codex commit regex. This is a clean fourth pass.

Two correctness issues and two documentation gaps are worth resolving before merge.

---

### Correctness

**1. `observeCopilotRequest` doesn't paginate — can miss fresh events on busy PRs**

`main.go:516-577`:

```go
timelineEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf(
    "repos/%s/issues/%d/timeline?per_page=100", ...)
data, err := runner.Run(ctx, "gh", "api", timelineEndpoint)  // no --paginate

reviewsEndpoint := fmt.Sprintf(
    "repos/%s/pulls/%d/reviews?per_page=100", ...)
reviewData, err := runner.Run(ctx, "gh", "api", reviewsEndpoint)  // no --paginate
```

Both calls fetch a single page (≤100 results). GitHub's timeline and reviews APIs return in chronological order, so for a PR with >100 events (a long-running canary PR easily has this) the fresh `review_requested` or `copilot_work_started` event lives past offset 100 and is silently skipped, causing `requestGitHubReviewer` to return `"GitHub did not record the request"`. By contrast, `fetchReviews` in the observation flow at `observe.go:119` correctly uses `--paginate --slurp`. The same fix applies here: `"gh", "api", "--paginate", "--slurp", timelineEndpoint` (with a wrapping `[][]T` decode). [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20cmd%2Freview%2Fmain.go%20in%20observeCopilotRequest%2C%20change%20both%20gh%20api%20calls%20(timeline%20at%20line%20~521%20and%20reviews%20at%20line%20~553)%20from%20single-page%20fetches%20to%20paginated%20fetches%20using%20--paginate%20--slurp%2C%20matching%20how%20fetchReviews%20in%20observe.go%3A119%20works%2C%20and%20update%20the%20unmarshal%20targets%20to%20the%20corresponding%20%5B%5D%5B%5DT%20slice-of-pages%20types&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

**2. `github-copilot` is in `actorMatches` but not in `isCopilotLogin` — asymmetry across the request/observe boundary**

`observe.go:299`:
```go
"copilot": {"copilot", "copilot-pull-request-reviewer", "github-copilot"},
```

`main.go:603-608`:
```go
func isCopilotLogin(login string) bool {
    switch strings.ToLower(login) {
    case "copilot", "copilot-pull-request-reviewer",
        "copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]":
        return true
    }
    return false
}
```

`"github-copilot"` is recognized for observation (via `actorMatches`) but not for requests (via `isCopilotLogin`). If GitHub presents `"github-copilot"` in a `requested_reviewers` response body, `responseRecordsReviewer` returns `(false, nil)` (since `isCopilotLogin("github-copilot")` is false), leading to `observeCopilotRequest`, which also uses `isCopilotLogin` on timeline and reviews events and would again miss `"github-copilot"`. The result is a false `"did not record the request"` failure even though the request succeeded. Since `actorMatches` already knows this alias and `TestActorMatchesConfiguredReviewerAliases` explicitly covers it, adding `"github-copilot"` to `isCopilotLogin` closes the gap with no behavior change for the common case. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20cmd%2Freview%2Fmain.go%20in%20isCopilotLogin%20around%20line%20603%2C%20add%20%22github-copilot%22%20to%20the%20switch%20case%20to%20match%20the%20alias%20set%20already%20recognized%20by%20actorMatches%20in%20observe.go%3A299%2C%20and%20add%20a%20corresponding%20assertion%20to%20TestActorMatchesConfiguredReviewerAliases%20or%20a%20new%20test%20to%20cover%20this%20path&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

---

### Design

**3. Late-cycle park unconditionally overrides raised-tier escalation — priority undocumented**

`policy.go:145-156`:

```go
if raisedTier(plan, input.CurrentTier) {
    action = reviewroute.ActionEscalate    // set unconditionally
    reasons = append(reasons, "tier_increased")
}
if input.Cycle > 3 && (input.CurrentTier != "T3" || ...) {
    action = reviewroute.ActionPark        // also unconditional — overrides Escalate
    reasons = append(reasons, "late_cycle_requires_t3_rationale")
}
```

The late-cycle guard can silently demote `ActionEscalate` to `ActionPark`. The final two checks are explicitly guarded with `action == ActionContinue`, but these two are not, creating an implicit priority chain: `Park > Escalate > Stop > Continue`. The priority is defensible (T3 rationale must be provided before any further action, including escalation), but a reader adjusting the ordering would not know this. A short comment at the late-cycle block naming the override intent would prevent a silent behavior change from reordering. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20cmd%2Freview%2Finternal%2Fpolicy%2Fpolicy.go%20around%20line%20145%2C%20add%20a%20comment%20before%20the%20%22if%20input.Cycle%20%3E%203%22%20block%20explaining%20that%20this%20check%20fires%20unconditionally%20and%20intentionally%20overrides%20ActionEscalate%20-%20T3%20rationale%20is%20required%20before%20any%20further%20action%20including%20escalation%2C%20and%20the%20tier_increased%20reason%20code%20is%20still%20preserved%20in%20reasons&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

**4. `proofCloses` hard-codes T3 exclusion without a comment**

`policy.go:272-276`:

```go
func proofCloses(plan reviewroute.Plan, tier string, critical bool, proofRef string) bool {
    if critical || !plan.Requirements.AllowProofSubstitution || strings.TrimSpace(proofRef) == "" {
        return false
    }
    return tier == "T0" || tier == "T1" || tier == "T2"
}
```

The canary policy sets T3 `allow_proof_substitution: false`, making the tier guard currently redundant. But a future operator adding a custom policy with T3 `allow_proof_substitution: true` would expect it to enable proof-close and would find it silently inactive. The `proofSubstitutesPanel` function above has a `// Proof substitution closes a rereview only after...` comment explaining its cycle-2 guard; `proofCloses` deserves the same treatment for its T3 exclusion — a one-line comment that names the invariant and why. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20cmd%2Freview%2Finternal%2Fpolicy%2Fpolicy.go%20in%20proofCloses%20around%20line%20276%2C%20add%20a%20comment%20before%20the%20return%20statement%20explaining%20that%20T3%20findings%20always%20require%20human-in-the-loop%20reviewer%20closure%20and%20cannot%20be%20proof-substituted%20even%20if%20allow_proof_substitution%20is%20set%20in%20the%20policy%2C%20matching%20the%20style%20of%20the%20cycle-guard%20comment%20in%20proofSubstitutesPanel&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

---

### Positive observations

All three prior rounds of review feedback is correctly applied:
- `actorMatches("copilot", "Copilot")` is fixed; `TestActorMatchesConfiguredReviewerAliases` explicitly covers all four reviewers including `"Copilot"` and `"github-copilot"` aliases
- `codexReviewedCommit` regex requires exactly `{40}` hex chars; `TestCleanCommentRequiresFullExactHead` verifies the abbreviated SHA is rejected
- `cleanComment` codex-specificity is documented at `observe.go:258-261`
- Operator precedence parentheses are explicit: `(1<<decision.Cycle)-1` at `reviewroute.go:517`, `(1<<input.Cycle)-1` at `policy.go:170`
- `proved_safe` missing `proof_ref` and `reviewer_closed` is caught at `reviewroute.go:434-440`
- `stale`-overwrites-`failed` priority comment is at `main.go:349-351`
- `runDecide` validates plan and input before `fetchPullRequest` (`main.go:635-640`); `TestDecideRefusesInvalidPlanBeforeNetwork` verifies zero network calls on invalid input

### Summary

All four findings from the fourth review pass are correctly addressed. This is a clean fifth pass. Two new issues are worth resolving before merge: a schema/runtime case inconsistency for `head_sha` that would silently break a schema-following agent, and a redundant observation loop that makes 6 paginated API calls in the Copilot fallback failure case.

---

### Correctness

**1. `head_sha` JSON schema pattern allows uppercase but the artifact join requires lowercase**

All four artifact schemas (`review-plan-v1.json`, `review-cycle-input-v1.json`, `review-request-v1.json`, `review-decision-v1.json`) specify `head_sha` with pattern `"^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$"` — accepting uppercase. But:

- Plan SHAs are always stored lowercase (`strings.ToLower(after.HeadRefOID)` at `main.go:156`)
- `validSHA` in `reviewroute.go:568-574` accepts uppercase via `hex.DecodeString`
- `policy.Decide` at `policy.go:124` joins plan and input with a case-sensitive struct comparison: `plan.Subject != input.Subject`

An agent that follows the schema literally and submits a `CycleInput` with an uppercase `head_sha` (valid by the schema) would receive `"review artifacts do not join at the exact plan and head"` — no indication that case normalization is required. The hidden invariant (lowercase-only at runtime) contradicts the schema's `[0-9a-fA-F]` allowance. `validLowerHex` at `reviewroute.go:583-596` already enforces lowercase for digest values — `validSHA` should do the same.

Fix: tighten all `head_sha`, `head_before`, and `head_after` patterns in the JSON schemas from `[0-9a-fA-F]{40}` to `[0-9a-f]{40}`, and update `validSHA` to match `validLowerHex`'s explicit lowercase enforcement. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20tighten%20all%20head_sha%2C%20head_before%2C%20and%20head_after%20patterns%20in%20the%20four%20JSON%20schemas%20under%20contracts%2Freviewroute%2Fschema%2F%20from%20%5B0-9a-fA-F%5D%7B40%7D%20to%20%5B0-9a-f%5D%7B40%7D%2C%20and%20update%20validSHA%20in%20contracts%2Freviewroute%2Freviewroute.go%20to%20enforce%20lowercase%20hex%20directly%20(matching%20validLowerHex%20style)%20instead%20of%20using%20hex.DecodeString%20which%20accepts%20uppercase&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

**2. `observeCopilotRequest` is called up to three times in the copilot login fallback loop**

`requestGitHubReviewer` at `main.go:477-507` loops over three copilot login forms. Each iteration that returns `recorded=false` from `responseRecordsReviewer` calls `observeCopilotRequest`, which makes two paginated API requests (timeline + reviews). In the common full-failure case (all three logins unrecorded), `observeCopilotRequest` is called three times — six API calls total. Since the underlying timeline and reviews state is the same regardless of which login form was used for the POST, the second and third observation calls return the same result as the first and add no signal.

The cleanest fix: on the first `observeCopilotRequest` call that returns `(_, false, nil)`, break the loop immediately rather than continuing to the next login. At that point the observation state is established — Copilot has not picked up the request — and no further login form will change that. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20cmd%2Freview%2Fmain.go%20in%20requestGitHubReviewer%2C%20after%20the%20observeCopilotRequest%20call%20returns%20(_%2C%20false%2C%20nil)%20(not%20observed%20and%20no%20error)%2C%20break%20the%20login%20loop%20immediately%20instead%20of%20continuing%20to%20the%20next%20login%20form%2C%20since%20the%20timeline%20and%20reviews%20state%20is%20shared%20across%20all%20login%20attempts%20and%20the%20subsequent%20observeCopilotRequest%20calls%20would%20return%20the%20same%20result&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

---

### Design

**3. `validSHA` uses `hex.DecodeString` while `validLowerHex` manually enforces lowercase — inconsistent validation philosophy for hex content**

`reviewroute.go:568-574` (`validSHA`) accepts both cases via `hex.DecodeString`; `reviewroute.go:583-596` (`validLowerHex`) enforces lowercase with explicit `'a'–'f'` range checks. Both are used for hex content: `validSHA` for commit SHAs, `validLowerHex` for `sha256:` digests. A reader or maintainer adding a new hex field would have two incompatible templates to choose from, with no documentation of why the inconsistency exists. Unifying to the `validLowerHex` approach (or renaming `validSHA` to `validLowerSHA`) would make the case requirement explicit and consistent. This is addressed by the fix in finding #1 above.

---

### Positive observations

All four fourth-pass findings are correctly resolved in the current code:
- Both copilot observation endpoints now use `--paginate --slurp` (`main.go:541, 559`); `TestRequestAcceptsFreshCopilotTimelineEvidence` explicitly verifies the pagination flags
- `isCopilotLogin` at `main.go:631-638` includes `"github-copilot"`, matching `actorMatches`'s alias set; `TestObserveCopilotRequestAcceptsExactHeadReviewOnLaterPage` covers a multi-page `github-copilot` review result
- Late-cycle park override priority is documented at `policy.go:146-147`: "parks before any further action, including a raised-tier escalation; the tier reason remains recorded"
- T3 proof-close exclusion is documented at `policy.go:278-279`: "T3 always requires reviewer closure, even if a custom policy mistakenly enables proof substitution for the tier"

Additional code-quality notes worth acknowledging:
- `TestRequestAcceptsFreshCopilotTimelineEvidence` explicitly rejects any non-paginated API call with `errors.New("Copilot evidence lookup must paginate")` — this is the right way to enforce the pagination invariant in tests
- `TestActorMatchesConfiguredReviewerAliases` now covers all four reviewers including `"Copilot"` and `"github-copilot"` for the copilot alias
- `TestCleanCommentRequiresFullExactHead` correctly rejects abbreviated SHA (`testHeadA[:10]`) and accepts the full 40-char value

The decision artifact alone is not sufficient for an execution engine to know which ones to re-request — it must cross-reference the panel evidence to filter already-completed reviewers out. This cross-artifact dependency has no test and no comment. **Claude finished @itsHabib's task in 6m 17s** —— [View job](https://github.com/itsHabib/workbench/actions/runs/30602676401)

---
### Review: feat(review): add opt-in exact-head tier-aware policy

- [x] Gather context and understand request
- [x] Read current code state (check 8th pass observations)
- [x] Read new commits since last review (`4e99892`, `cd49b1a`)
- [x] Analyze for any remaining or new issues
- [x] Post review findings

---

### Summary

This is a clean ninth pass. Both 8th-pass observations are correctly resolved. The `4e99892` commit tightens the `repo` pattern to `^[a-z0-9._-]+/[a-z0-9._-]+$` in all four schemas and adds a `validateSubject` lowercase guard in Go; the CLAUDE.md invariant now correctly reads "missing required reviewers and finding authors still in play." The `cd49b1a` commit adds the adversarial evidence binding cleanly — content-addressed digest, exact-head subject match, `adversarial_complete ↔ pass evidence` consistency check, and `localAdversarialComplete` for T0. Two correctness gaps and two test coverage gaps are worth addressing.

---

### Confirmed Resolved: 8th Pass Observations

**Observation 1 — `repo` schema pattern did not enforce lowercase**

Correctly addressed in `4e99892`. All four schemas now have `^[a-z0-9._-]+/[a-z0-9._-]+$`. `validateSubject` at `reviewroute.go:588-590` adds a Go-level check (`subject.Repo != strings.ToLower(subject.Repo)` → error). `TestDecideRejectsRepoCaseMismatch` fails at `ValidateCycleInput` before `Decide` because `validateSubject` now rejects the uppercase repo directly.

**Observation 2 — CLAUDE.md invariant "Later cycles target only finding authors still in play" was imprecise**

Correctly updated: `CLAUDE.md:38-39` now reads "Later cycles target only missing required reviewers and finding authors still in play."

---

### Correctness

**1. `adversarial_complete ↔ pass evidence` constraint is in Go but not in the JSON schema**

`ValidateCycleInput` at `reviewroute.go:381-384` correctly enforces:

```go
evidenceComplete := input.AdversarialEvidence != nil &&
    input.AdversarialEvidence.Result == "pass"
if input.AdversarialComplete != evidenceComplete {
    return errors.New("reviewroute: adversarial_complete must match pass evidence")
}
```

But `review-cycle-input-v1.json` has `adversarial_complete` and `adversarial_evidence` as separate required fields with no `allOf` constraint linking them. An agent following only the JSON schema can produce `adversarial_complete: true` with `adversarial_evidence: null` — passes schema, fails `ValidateCycleInput` with a non-specific error ("adversarial_complete must match pass evidence" rather than pointing at the null evidence). The `proved_safe` case was handled with an explicit `allOf` in both artifact schemas — the same treatment would close this gap and give schema-level diagnostics consistent with how the finding-state invariant is documented. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20contracts%2Freviewroute%2Fschema%2Freview-cycle-input-v1.json%2C%20add%20an%20allOf%20entry%20(after%20the%20existing%20properties%20block%2C%20at%20the%20root%20object%20level)%3A%20if%20adversarial_complete%20is%20const%20true%2C%20then%20adversarial_evidence%20must%20be%20of%20type%20object%20with%20result%20const%20%22pass%22.%20This%20mirrors%20the%20proved_safe%20allOf%20constraint%20in%20the%20findings%20array%20and%20closes%20the%20gap%20between%20JSON%20schema%20and%20Go%20layer%20enforcement&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

**2. `localAdversarialComplete` and `AdversarialVerification` blockers fire in the same `blockers()` call but share a single `AdversarialEvidence` field**

`blockers()` at `policy.go:204-209`:

```go
if plan.Requirements.LocalAdversarial && !localAdversarialComplete(input) {
    reasons = append(reasons, "local_adversarial_incomplete")
}
if plan.Requirements.AdversarialVerification && !input.AdversarialComplete {
    reasons = append(reasons, "adversarial_incomplete")
}
```

`localAdversarialComplete` checks `Source == "local"`. `AdversarialVerification` only checks `AdversarialComplete == true`. If a future tier sets both requirements simultaneously, a `source == "adversarial-workflow"` evidence satisfies `AdversarialVerification` but not `LocalAdversarial` — which is defensible. But `cleanInput` in tests would silently override the `local` evidence with `adversarial-workflow` (second `if` block at `policy_test.go:422-429` overwrites the first), producing a test helper that doesn't satisfy `LocalAdversarial` for such a tier. The canary policy has no tier with both flags set, so no current test is affected. A one-line comment in `cleanInput` noting the mutual-exclusivity assumption would prevent silent test failures for future policy configurations.

---

### Test Coverage

**3. T3 adversarial verification path has no dedicated test symmetrical to T0's**

`TestT0RequiresLocalAdversarialPass` and `TestT0RejectsNonlocalAdversarialPass` directly exercise T0's `local_adversarial` requirement. T3 has `adversarial_verification: true`, which maps to the `"adversarial_incomplete"` blocker path in `blockers()` — but there is no test that explicitly verifies:

- T3 without adversarial evidence → `"adversarial_incomplete"` reason code and `ActionContinue` decision
- T3 decision carries the bound adversarial evidence (analogous to `TestT0DecisionBindsLocalAdversarialEvidence`)

Every call to `cleanInput(plan, cycle)` for T3 sets `AdversarialComplete = true` with `source == "adversarial-workflow"`, so the blocker never fires in any existing T3 test. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20workbench%20on%20branch%20codex%2Ftier-aware-review-policy%2C%20in%20cmd%2Freview%2Finternal%2Fpolicy%2Fpolicy_test.go%2C%20add%20two%20tests%3A%20(1)%20TestT3RequiresAdversarialVerification%3A%20build%20a%20T3%20plan%20with%20routedPlan%2C%20call%20cleanInput(plan%2C1)%20then%20set%20AdversarialComplete%3Dfalse%2C%20AdversarialEvidence%3Dnil%2C%20call%20Decide%20and%20verify%20decision.ReasonCodes%20contains%20%22adversarial_incomplete%22%3B%20(2)%20TestT3DecisionBindsAdversarialEvidence%3A%20verify%20that%20decision.AdversarialEvidence%20matches%20input.AdversarialEvidence%20exactly%2C%20mirroring%20TestT0DecisionBindsLocalAdversarialEvidence&repo=itsHabib/workbench)

**4. `TestAdversarialCompleteRequiresBoundPassEvidence` doesn't exercise the cross-subject case for `result == "escalate"`**

`TestAdversarialCompleteRequiresBoundPassEvidence` in `reviewroute_test.go:213-256` correctly tests: unbound completion, confidence mutation, and `result: "escalate"` claiming completion. The final assertion at line 252-255 checks a cross-head `Subject.HeadSHA` mismatch with `AdversarialComplete = false` — but doesn't verify that the same cross-head evidence with `AdversarialComplete = false` and `result == "escalate"` is rejected because `evidence.Subject != subject`. The test currently changes `Subject.HeadSHA` after setting `result = "escalate"` and `AdversarialComplete = false`, so `ValidateCycleInput` fails at the `evidenceComplete` consistency check (`false != false` is false → no error there) — it fails at `validateAdversarialEvidence` due to the subject mismatch. This is correct behavior but the test comment is absent, making the assertion intent unclear. A comment on the final assertion block would help future readers understand which validation is under test.

---

### Positive Observations

All prior round findings are correctly resolved:

- `codexReviewedCommit` regex uses `[0-9a-f]{40}` with `strings.EqualFold` comparison; `TestCleanCommentRequiresFullExactHead` covers abbreviated and uppercase rejection
- `proved_safe` requires `reviewer_closed` or `proof_ref` in `validateFindingState` and in the JSON schema `allOf`
- `stale`-overwrites-`failed` priority comment is at `main.go:349-351`
- `runDecide` validates plan and input before `fetchPullRequest`; `TestDecideRefusesInvalidPlanBeforeNetwork` asserts zero network calls on invalid input
- All four schemas use `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` for SHA fields and `^[a-z0-9._-]+/[a-z0-9._-]+$` for repo
- `validateSubject` enforces lowercase repo at the Go layer (`reviewroute.go:588`)
- `sortedUnique` is package-private; `validSHA` delegates to `validLowerHex`; `TestValidSHARequiresLowercase` confirms uppercase rejection
- Late-cycle park priority comment at `policy.go:148-150`; `proofSubstitutesPanel` cycle-2 guard comment; `proofCloses` T3 exclusion comment
- `observeAfter.IsZero()` guard ensures a single `observeCopilotRequest` call; pagination uses `--paginate --slurp`
- `actorMatches` copilot alias set matches `isCopilotLogin`; `TestActorMatchesConfiguredReviewerAliases` covers all four reviewers

For the new adversarial evidence binding specifically:
- `validateAdversarialEvidence` enforces exact-head subject match (struct equality), non-empty source, valid result enum, 0..1 confidence, and sha256 digest — all correct
- `cloneAdversarialEvidence` correctly deep-copies the evidence into the decision rather than sharing the pointer
- `TestT0DecisionBindsLocalAdversarialEvidence` verifies T0's local evidence is bound into the decision artifact
- `TestT0RejectsNonlocalAdversarialPass` verifies that `source == "adversarial-workflow"` fails `localAdversarialComplete` for T0
- `TestAdversarialCompleteRequiresBoundPassEvidence` exercises unbound completion, confidence digest mutation, and `result: "escalate"` claiming completion

The design is sound. Findings 1 and 3 are the most actionable before merge.

### Review: feat(review): add opt-in exact-head tier-aware policy

- [x] Gather context and understand request
- [x] Read current code state (CLAUDE.md, all four JSON schemas, observe.go, policy.go, reviewroute.go, main.go)
- [x] Check 8th pass observations against current code
- [x] Analyze for any new issues

---

### Summary

This is a clean ninth pass. Both 8th-pass observations are correctly resolved. One micro-gap is noted below for completeness; it is not blocking.

---

### Confirmed Resolved: 8th Pass Observations

**Observation 1 — `CLAUDE.md` invariant "Later cycles target only finding authors still in play" was imprecise**

Correctly addressed. `cmd/review/CLAUDE.md:38-39` now reads:

```
- Later cycles target only missing required reviewers and finding authors still
  in play.
```

Both routing sources are now captured in the invariant.

**Observation 2 — `repo` JSON schema pattern did not enforce lowercase**

Correctly addressed, and beyond what was observed:

- All four JSON schemas now use `^[a-z0-9._-]+/[a-z0-9._-]+$` for every `repo` field (`review-plan-v1.json:47`, `review-cycle-input-v1.json:13`, `review-decision-v1.json:14`, `review-request-v1.json:14`)
- `validateSubject` at `reviewroute.go:588-590` adds an explicit Go-level lowercase check: `if subject.Repo != strings.ToLower(subject.Repo) { return errors.New("reviewroute: subject repo must be lowercase") }`

An agent submitting an uppercase `repo` now fails at validation with a specific, informative error — not the misleading "review artifacts do not join at the exact plan and head" from before.

---

### Micro-gap (non-blocking)

**`enabled_repositories` policy schema pattern and `validateUnique` allow case-colliding entries**

`review-policy-v1.json:13` uses `^[^/]+/[^/]+$` for `enabled_repositories` items — allowing mixed-case. `validateUnique` in `reviewroute.go:665-677` uses exact-string comparison, so `"OWNER/REPO"` and `"owner/repo"` are treated as distinct and both pass. Since `enabled()` uses `strings.EqualFold`, both entries resolve to the same repo match.

In practice this requires a policy operator to intentionally write two differently-cased entries for the same repo, which is vanishingly unlikely. The `EqualFold` choice in `enabled()` is correct for human-configured input. This is a documentation gap rather than a correctness issue — a short comment on `validateUnique`'s case-sensitive behavior at the `enabled_repository` call site would signal that case-folded duplicates are not caught. Not blocking.

---

### Positive Observations

All prior findings from eight rounds are correctly present and tested in the current code. Key strengths worth noting on this pass:

- `validateSubject` lowercase enforcement (`reviewroute.go:588-590`) closes the schema-contract gap decisively — the error is specific and actionable rather than surfacing as an artifact-join failure deep in `Decide`
- `cd49b1a fix(review): bind adversarial evidence to decisions` correctly validates `decision.AdversarialEvidence.Subject == decision.Subject` via `validateAdversarialEvidence` in `ValidateDecision` (`reviewroute.go:490`), preventing evidence from a different PR head being carried into the decision artifact
- `dbd3711 fix(review): target only missing panel reviewers` correctly factors `missingRequiredReviewers` so both `blockers()` and `validatePanelCompletion()` share the same computation without either needing to know the other's routing context
- `e020c87 fix(review): require lowercase Codex review heads` correctly narrows `codexReviewedCommit` to `[0-9a-f]{40}`, matching every other SHA constraint in the codebase
- `c26bd03 fix(review): restore scoped guidance pointer` correctly restores the AGENTS.md canonical pointer that caused the hygiene failure

The design — content-addressed plan IDs, two-fence head checks at all four phases, `strictJSON` with `DisallowUnknownFields` + EOF double-decode, `writeAtomic`, hard-coded `safePanel` fallback, and `ValidatePolicy` referential integrity — is all correctly implemented and tested. The contracts leaf constraint is respected.

---

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reserve “resolved” logs for decision exits**

When `gate resolve` exits 4 after an internal, state, or audit failure, `ingest.execRunner` intentionally returns that exit status with `err == nil`, so this condition emits `resolved ... gate_exit=4` even though no clean decision landed. This makes the new success-path log misleading precisely when an operator needs to retry or investigate; emit “resolved” only for Gate’s 0–3 decision space and log exit 4 as a failure.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L38-L39](https://github.com/itsHabib/workbench/blob/748dbd69303d97a798dcd1e75510450f144f61b5/AGENTS.md#L38-L39)

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move accepted logging off the acknowledgment path**

When stderr or its log collector is slow or blocked, `log.Printf` can block before `writeAck` and before `s.process` is started; because the standard logger serializes writes, one stalled background log can also hold up every subsequent callback here. Those callbacks can miss Slack's ~3-second acknowledgment window while their authoritative resolutions have not even begun, causing retries or lost taps, so record acceptance only after the acknowledgment path has returned or via nonblocking/background logging.
